clue.text: Sign, accepting current hire

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the hire word holds the current inside it

parts.note: to charter a boat or plane is to hire it
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A notice taking on a temporary worker while the electricity bill comes due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts AC inside CHARTER, splitting it after CHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A written letter or symbol, such as a Chinese ideogram, is a sign of this kind.

clue.text: Ring company accountant about drink

indicators.note: about means around, so the accountant goes round the ring

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone phones a firm's accountant about a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CA around O to make COA, after CO. 'Ring' reads as phoning but is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot chocolate made from powdered cacao is a familiar warm drink.

clue.text: Say I'm into uncontrolled hostility

indicators.note: uncontrolled letters run wild, so the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A speaker admits to being caught up in unchecked aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncontrolled' rearranges SAY I'M INTO. 'into' looks like a container signal but is part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is strong ill will or enmity, which is hostility.

clue.text: Connected with data file if replaced

indicators.note: replaced means put back in different places, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A data file gets linked to something else if it is swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges DATA FILE IF.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm affiliated with another is officially linked or associated with it.

clue.text: During half-term refined clear syrup

indicators.note: during means within, so the jumbled letters go inside the halved word
half of the word means its first two of four letters
refined means processed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A half-term treat of refined clear syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes TE from TERM; 'refined' rearranges CLEAR into REACL, and 'During' sets it inside TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is the dark sticky syrup left from refining sugar.

clue.text: Crawler put hat material on top

indicators.note: on top in a down clue places the material piece above the hat piece

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Someone sewing material onto the top of a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE as slang for a hat is dated British usage; REP sits on top of it in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes and lizards are creatures that move low along the ground, so one is a crawler.

clue.text: Rash drunk has little money for bitter

indicators.note: a drunk person is scrambled, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

parts.note: P is a penny, the smallest unit of British money

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy and broke ends up resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges RASH into SHAR, and P follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter wind or a bitter remark is cutting and keen, which is what sharp also describes.

clue.text: Erected excellent notice

indicators.note: erected means set upright, so in a down answer the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: tops is slang for excellent, the very best

explanation.surface: Someone put up a first-rate sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erected' turns TOPS upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see it, to notice it.

clue.text: Expect a head waiter on a small island

indicators.note: the head of the word is its first letter

parts.note: an ait is a small river island, especially on the Thames

explanation.surface: Anticipating a head waiter working on a little island.
explanation.walkthrough: AIT (also spelt eyot) is a British word for a little island in a river. 'head waiter' looks like one job title.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to wait for it, expecting it to come.

clue.text: Stopped parking on grass outside exit

parts.note: P is the sign for parking

indicators.note: outside means the grass word goes around the exit word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a vent is an outlet, a way out for air or smoke

explanation.surface: A ban on parking on the grass outside the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts REED around VENT to make REVENTED, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it happening.

clue.text: College head, if he becomes principal

indicators.note: the head of the word is its first letter
the words turn into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A college head who has risen to be its principal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' rearranges IF HE into HIEF, after C from 'College head'. 'College head' and 'principal' both look like job titles; only 'principal' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal as an adjective means main or foremost, the same as the adjective chief.

clue.text: Page One is about spying

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the three words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A newspaper's front page carries a story on espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it tells you to rearrange PAGE ONE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is the gathering of secrets, which is what this word names as a noun.

clue.text: Furious PC at police assembly

indicators.note: the letters are put together in a new arrangement, as parts are in an assembly

explanation.surface: A constable is angry at a police meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' reads as a gathering of officers, but it signals rearranging PC AT POLICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone apoplectic is overcome with anger, close to having a fit from rage.

clue.text: Some nasty ear or eye trouble

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An unpleasant ear infection, or perhaps a problem with the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'or', which is the link joining wordplay to definition; the definition is 'eye trouble' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen infected gland on the eyelid is a common, minor eye complaint.

clue.text: If some turn over it will be a calamity

indicators.note: over as in turned over, so the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Disaster will follow if some people are overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges IF SOME TURN; 'turn' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfortune is a stroke of bad luck, a disaster or calamity.

clue.text: Weather cold and I'm slow to come round

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: the slow word comes round, meaning it encloses the next piece

parts.note: a late train is a slow one, behind time
I'm gives the letters I and M as written

explanation.surface: A grumbler complains about chilly weather and being slow to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come round' wraps LATE around IM, giving LIMATE after C.
explanation.definitionFit: The climate of a region is its typical weather pattern over time.

clue.text: Goat, when first caught, can rip or chew up

indicators.note: first places this letter before everything else

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: chewing up mangles something, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A goat, once caught, can tear or chew things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chew up' rearranges CAN RIP OR into APRICORN, and 'first' puts C ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign represented by a sea-goat is named this.

clue.text: Clear disreputable bar, returning around ten

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the bar word is read backwards

parts.note: a dive is a seedy, disreputable drinking place

indicators.note: around here means turned about, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone clears out of a seedy pub, coming back at about ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns DIVE into EVID; 'around' then jumbles TEN into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident is plain to see, obvious, in the same way something clear is.

clue.text: They inspect cutter rejected by colliers

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the cutter word is read backwards

parts.note: an axe is a cutting tool
colliers are coal miners

explanation.surface: Inspectors find a cutting tool turned down by coal miners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns AXE into EXA, followed by MINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners are people who check or test, inspecting work or candidates.

clue.text: Pam heard why, in hospital, it's punishment

indicators.note: in places the sounded letter inside the name

parts.note: Pam is taken as written

indicators.note: heard tells you to take the sound of the next word rather than its spelling

parts.note: the word why is said exactly like the letter Y
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Pam is asked in hospital why she is being punished.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y from 'heard why' goes inside PAM to make PAYM, and ENT follows. The definition works because a penalty paid out is a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting one's due reward or penalty is a payment; the punishment is what is paid for wrongdoing.

clue.text: War Office fellow notified about double

indicators.note: about means around, so the notified word encloses the others

parts.note: to be told something is to be notified of it
WO is the abbreviation for the War Office

explanation.surface: A War Office official is informed about a duplicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places TOLD around WO and F.
explanation.definitionFit: Twofold means having two parts, the same as double.

clue.text: Cheat failure without fear, working on

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the failure word goes round the rest

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to work

indicators.note: working on something means reshaping it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A con artist fails but works on regardless, without fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working on' rearranges FEAR into EFRA, and 'without' (meaning outside) puts DUD around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To defraud someone is to swindle them out of money, a form of cheating.

clue.text: Degrades bachelors, raising children without

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the children word goes round
raising in a down clue lifts the word so it reads upward

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring
BAs are holders of the bachelor of arts degree

explanation.surface: Unmarried men lose dignity by bringing up children without help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns SEED into DEES, and 'without' (outside) puts it around BAS. 'bachelors' are degree holders, not single men.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase something is to lower its quality or standing, which degrades it.

clue.text: Said I owe volunteers a very small amount

indicators.note: said tells you to take the sound of the next words, not their spelling

parts.note: the words I owe are said like the two letters I and O
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Someone admits a debt to unpaid helpers, but only a tiny sum.
explanation.walkthrough: IO is what 'I owe' sounds like; then TA.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth Greek letter is the smallest, so its name came to mean a tiny bit.

clue.text: Colour of can standing up, say

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: standing up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: The colour of a tin can left upright, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns EG into GE, after TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour, a tint.

clue.text: Projectile with which raider shot soldier

parts.note: a bomb is a missile that is thrown or dropped

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters of the word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A raider fires a missile at a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like firing but rearranges RAIDER into ARDIER, after BOMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardier is a junior rank of non-commissioned officer in the British artillery.

clue.text: Free ruler for cyclist?

parts.note: to rid is to free
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Asking whether a free ruler would suit a bike rider.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen. The question mark marks the definition as an example: a cyclist is one kind of person who rides.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on a bicycle is one who rides, an instance of the general word.

clue.text: Something which carries revolvers

parts.note: the revolvers are not guns but wheels, which turn on the rod that bears them

explanation.surface: A holster for pistols.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolvers' suggests handguns, but the things that revolve here are wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: This rod passes through the centre of wheels, bearing them as they spin.

clue.text: Outside broadcast on Sioux organisation is offensive

indicators.note: organising letters means arranging them anew, so these words are jumbled

parts.note: on is taken as written into the mix
Sioux, the Native American people, is taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV outside broadcast about a Sioux group is deemed offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges ON and SIOUX into NOXIOUS, after OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious behaviour is highly unpleasant, the kind that gives offence.

clue.text: Upset nude model quietly entering

indicators.note: the quiet letter goes into the rearranged word
to model something is to shape it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A nude model is upset when someone quietly walks into the studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' rearranges NUDE into UEND, and 'entering' puts P inside after U.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend a thing is to turn it upside down, to overturn or upset it.

clue.text: She takes key to church back in first

indicators.note: first says this piece comes before the rest
back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: in is taken as written before being turned round
E is a musical key
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A woman brings a key to the church and is first back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IN into NI, which 'first' puts ahead of E and CE. 'takes' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a female relative, a brother's or sister's daughter, so she fits.

clue.text: One obeying doctor's orders?

parts.note: not a patient but a pharmacist, who carries out the doctor's prescriptions by making them up

explanation.surface: A dutiful patient does as the doctor says.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a compliant patient; the person who follows the doctor's written orders is the chemist making up the prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist who makes up prescriptions dispenses medicine as the doctor directs.
